title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. k (written 'h' throughout) is a base ring. P is a k-additive category of complexes L_· of finite free k-modules (the 'parfaits'). It contains the 'disk' complexes C^i_· (k --id--> k, sitting in degrees i, i+1) and the 'sphere' complexes Psi^i_· (k in degree i). The disks assemble into a complex-object C^· in P, and Psi^i = Ker(C^i -> C^{i+1}) is a Sigma-kernel. Sigma is a class of degreewise split short exact sequences in P. B is an additive category with a class of exact sequences in which these Sigma-kernels exist.

Two functors are compared:
- rho: Hom_{k,Sigma-ex}(P,B) -> C(B), rho(F) = F(C^·), the complex in B obtained by evaluating F on the disk complex-object.
- sigma: C(B) -> Hom_{k,Sigma-ex}(P,B), sigma(C^·)(L_·) = Hom^·_k(L-check, C^·). This is a 'nerve'/co-Yoneda functor, built using L^· ≅ Hom(L_·, C^·).

The previous page established the adjunction formula Hom(rho F, C^·) ≅ Hom(F, sigma C^·) by unwinding natural transformations 'fonctoriels en L'.

On this page:
1. Grothendieck writes down the unit u: F -> sigma rho F, natural in F. He presents the partial adjunction map Hom(rho F, C^·) -> Hom(F, sigma C^·) as the composite Hom(rho F, C) -> Hom(sigma rho F, sigma C) -> Hom(F, sigma C), the second step being beta |-> beta o u. He states that showing this is an isomorphism is an easy verification.
2. He checks the counit rho sigma C^· -> C^·. Here rho(sigma C^·) = {sigma(C^·)(C^·_i)}_i, and sigma(C^·)(C_i) = Hom_k(C_i, C^·) = C^i. So the counit is an isomorphism, hence sigma is fully faithful ('pleinement fidèle').
3. He concludes that there is a fully faithful embedding sigma: C(B) -> Hom_{k,Sigma-ex}(P,B), inside all k-linear functors. 'Sigma-ex' means the functors that send Sigma-sequences to (left?) exact sequences.
4. He asks for the essential image: is it all Sigma-exact functors? It consists exactly of the F for which the unit u is an isomorphism.

The next page proves u is an isomorphism:
- on the C^i, directly;
- on the Psi^i, via F(Ker) = Ker F(...), which is where Sigma-exactness is used;
- on general bounded L, by induction on the length, writing L as a fibre product of a truncation L' and (C^p)^r over (Psi^{p+1})^r.

So the result is an equivalence: complexes in B are the same as Sigma-left-exact k-linear functors on finite free complexes. This is an Eilenberg–Watts / Kan-extension style representation theorem. It presumably serves to transport functorial and multiplicative structures on perfect complexes in the dévissage project.
errors: No mathematical error. The map 'alpha |-> alpha o u' as transcribed is really the composite alpha |-> sigma(alpha) o u, consistent with the dashed factorisation through Hom(sigma rho F, sigma C).
'C(C^·)_i' in the transcription should read C^i.

The essential-image claim (all Sigma-exact functors) is left open on this page and settled on the next page by dévissage. That argument implicitly needs F to commute with finite sums and Sigma-kernels, which Sigma-exactness provides.

ideas.what: Adjunction rho -| sigma between Sigma-exact k-linear functors on finite free complexes and complexes in B; unit/counit check; counit iso implies the right adjoint is fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Nerve–realization / co-Yoneda adjunction; Eilenberg–Watts-type representation of complexes as left exact functors
ideas.where_published: Similar Yoneda/representability techniques pervade SGA 4 Exp. I; this specific statement is not known to be published

ideas.what: Description of the essential image as the objects where the unit is an isomorphism, with the question whether it is all Sigma-exact functors
ideas.modern_name: Essential image of a fully faithful right adjoint

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine adjunction verification inside a representation theorem whose general shape (complexes = exact functors on perfect complexes via disks and spheres) is folklore. It is of interest only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished dévissage project, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'h' is Grothendieck's k (base ring): Hom_k, Hom_{k,Sigma-ex}, Hom_{k-lin}.
Line 3 likely reads 'homomorphisme fonctoriel en F, d'où l'homomorphisme d'adjonction partielle'.
'sigma est pl. fid.' = 'pleinement fidèle'; later 'une inclusion pleinement fidèle C(B)^· --sigma--> Hom_{k,Sigma-ex} ⊂ Hom_{k-lin}'.

'Quelle est l'image essentielle de B^·? (On donne des exemples ... de foncteurs dans l'image ...) est-ce tout Hom_{k,Sigma-ex}? Elle est formée des F telles que F -> sigma rho(F) soit un iso. Or on a -'
'Sigma-sex' probably abbreviates functors sending Sigma-sequences to (left) exact sequences; the parallel phrase on the previous page is 'suites exactes à g[auche]'.
